title: Wan fun control reference image ignored
body:
Testing the example control workflow. Connecting the reference image to the wan empty embeds does nothing.

In other words the output is the same with the default connections or with reference image, like the reference image is completely ignored.
author: luxdelux7

comments.body:
> Testing the example control workflow. Connecting the reference image to the wan empty embeds does nothing.
> 
> In other words the output is the same with the default connections or with reference image, like the reference image is completely ignored.

You don't connect it to the empty, that's just for T2V, you connect it straight to the sampler when using reference image.

Ah thank you. I was stupidly just connecting to the empty embeds as the note was above it.

It indeed works! Awesome. Now to test further.

satisfaction_conditions: Clear instructions on the correct connection point for the reference image in the control workflow
Explanation of the distinction between Text-to-Video (T2V) connections and reference image connections
Simple, direct guidance that corrects the user's workflow configuration

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

# ComfyUI wrapper nodes for [WanVideo](https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.1)

# WORK IN PROGRESS

# Installation
1. Clone this repo into `custom_nodes` folder.
2. Install dependencies: `pip install -r requirements.txt`
   or if you use the portable install, run this in ComfyUI_windows_portable -folder:

  `python_embeded\python.exe -m pip install -r ComfyUI\custom_nodes\ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper\requirements.txt`

## Models

https://huggingface.co/Kijai/WanVideo_comfy/tree/main

Text encoders to `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders`

Transformer to `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models`

Vae to `ComfyUI/models/vae`

name: Publish to Comfy registry
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - "pyproject.toml"

permissions:
  issues: write

jobs:
  publish-node:
    name: Publish Custom Node to registry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'kijai' }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Publish Custom Node
        uses: Comfy-Org/publish-node-action@v1
        with:
          ## Add your own personal access token to your Github Repository secrets and reference it here.
          personal_access_token: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

dockerfile:
FROM python:3.10-slim

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install git and other dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    git \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the ComfyUI repository (needed as the custom node is built for ComfyUI)
RUN git clone https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI.git

# Create the custom_nodes directory
RUN mkdir -p ComfyUI/custom_nodes

# Clone the WanVideoWrapper repository into custom_nodes
WORKDIR /app/ComfyUI/custom_nodes
RUN git clone https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper.git

# Checkout the specific commit mentioned in the issue
WORKDIR /app/ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper
RUN git checkout ac3f2859931513181f1c3ceaaacd8bce6c4f4889

# Install ComfyUI dependencies
WORKDIR /app/ComfyUI
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

# Install WanVideoWrapper dependencies
WORKDIR /app/ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

# Create directories for models that would be needed
RUN mkdir -p /app/ComfyUI/models/text_encoders \
    /app/ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models \
    /app/ComfyUI/models/vae

# Set the working directory back to the ComfyUI root
WORKDIR /app/ComfyUI

# The container is now ready for use
# Note to users: You'll need to mount or copy the model files into the appropriate directories
# - Text encoders to /app/ComfyUI/models/text_encoders
# - Transformer to /app/ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models
# - Vae to /app/ComfyUI/models/vae
# Models can be downloaded from https://huggingface.co/Kijai/WanVideo_comfy/tree/main

# Default command - can be overridden when running the container
CMD ["python", "-m", "main"]
